new_public_evidence.source: Howard, Ramdas, McAuliffe, Sekhon, Time-uniform, nonparametric, nonasymptotic confidence sequences
new_public_evidence.result: Empirical-Bernstein confidence sequences are valid uniformly over time for bounded adapted observations around average conditional means, with predictable variance proxies. The same framework explicitly supports inverse-probability-weighted estimators under past-dependent assignment probabilities.

new_public_evidence.source: Waudby-Smith and Ramdas, Estimating means of bounded random variables by betting
new_public_evidence.result: Predictable betting capital processes give anytime-valid bounded-mean confidence sequences and permit adaptive betting strategies without invalidating the test martingale.

new_public_evidence.source: Shin, Ramdas, Rinaldo, E-detectors: A Nonparametric Framework for Sequential Change Detection
new_public_evidence.result: e-SR/e-CUSUM detectors built from conditional e-values control average run length nonasymptotically and provide a principled fresh-start change layer after long pre-change prefixes.

derived_results.claim: For candidate q_j and current predictable proposal q_t, G_t(j)=H_t(base)-H_t(q_j) has conditional mean S_t(base)-S_t(q_j). The predictable exact range R_t(j)=max_i |W_i^2/q_t(i)(1/W_i-1/q_j(i))| makes Z_t=G_t/R_t lie in [-1,1]. Under no improvement, any predictable lambda_t in [0,1] yields a nonnegative supermartingale product of 1+lambda_t Z_t. Thus a finite family of proposal candidates can be promoted only after an anytime-valid, multiplicity-corrected gain certificate, without changing unbiasedness of the target risk estimator.

Pre-drift entry evidence certifies historical/average conditional gain and can remain large after proposal quality reverses. It cannot by itself certify the current second moment after drift. A separate harm process D_t=H_t(q_current)-H_t(base), normalized by its predictable exact range, supplies conditional e-values under no-harm; e-CUSUM can therefore trigger defensive fallback to base without relying on stale entry wealth.

A false harm alarm reverts to the base proposal, which preserves support and unbiasedness. Therefore its formal error semantics can be average-run-length rather than global PFA when the only consequence is lost efficiency; this allows a more aggressive harm threshold when slow fallback is costly.

In the synthetic stress, abrupt reversal was mostly neutralized by e-CUSUM fallback, but gradual degradation often remained harmful for tens of thousands of samples before alarm. A mixture/adaptive harm detector or continuous shrinkage toward base is required before treating the mechanism as robust to slow proxy decay.

engineering_update.scope: All measured values are from a synthetic 4096-branch rare-event abstraction with fixed candidate proposals and known base continuation law. They are engineering evidence only; the martingale/e-process validity claims come from the conditional-expectation derivations and cited sequential-inference results.

negative_or_scope_evidence: A stationary entry confidence process can be stale after nonstationary proxy drift; old evidence must not be interpreted as a current guarantee.
e-CUSUM controls average run length under no-harm, not the probability of ever causing a false fallback.
Rare labels make proposal-quality certification slow enough that conservative entry and fallback can consume most of the oracle variance gain.
Gradual proxy degradation is materially harder than abrupt reversal in the current detector configuration.

The exact-range normalization assumes candidate and current proposal probabilities are known and logged. If environment/tool transitions are proposed too, separate trajectory P/Q corrections remain necessary.
No LLM-agent or AGI capability conclusion follows.
frontier: Replace the fixed-lambda entry mixture with a Howard/Waudby-Smith variance-adaptive empirical-Bernstein or predictable-Kelly gate and measure certification delay under the same anytime familywise budget.
Construct a mixture/adaptive harm e-detector over effect scales and quantify gradual-drift fallback delay versus false fallback cost; compare with continuous epsilon shrinkage toward base.
Extend exact-range proposal comparison to dependent/systematic sibling resampling and random particle counts under proper weighting.
Find agent/LLM-specific multifidelity rare-event evaluation with explicit sparse high-fidelity target correction rather than treating an LLM judge as truth.
Characterize identifiable deployment-risk targets when environment/tool base likelihood ratios are unavailable.
exact_next_action: Implement a variance-adaptive entry certificate using the empirical-Bernstein confidence sequence for bounded gain G_t(j), with multiplicity correction over the fixed epsilon grid, and compare its certification time to the fixed-lambda mixture on the same rare-event paths. In parallel, build a two-or-more-scale harm e-detector (small persistent harm plus abrupt harm) and test whether gradual-drift median fallback delay can be cut materially without sacrificing the defensive-base safety semantics. Then continue dependent/random-count resampling and agent-specific multifidelity searches.
